A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, method, theoretical development, and experimental framework. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-classification and corruption-benchmark results, computational measurements, and experiments on sampling, feature learning, and hyperparameter transfer.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds a comparison with explicitly Wasserstein-regularized generalized variational inference in Figures S13–S14.

M1.justification: IBVI retains expected-loss training without an explicit divergence penalty, factorized Gaussian covariances, single-sample training, and the proposed variational maximal update parametrization. The added GVI objective is evaluated as a comparator.

E1.justification: The synthetic settings, MNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, TinyImageNet, and their corrupted counterparts are retained. The new GVI experiment uses MNIST, CIFAR10, MNISTC, and CIFAR10C, all already evaluated in v2.

E2.justification: GVI with a squared 2-Wasserstein penalty already appears in v2's Figure 1 toy comparison. v3 additionally evaluates low-rank GVI against Standard and IBVI on image benchmarks in Figures S13–S14. The existing temperature-scaling, Laplace, WSVI, SWAG, and ensemble comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section S3.3.4 adds a GVI evaluation across penalty weights 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, and 1.0, using the Section 5 setup. Existing splits, metrics, architectures, training budgets, and corruption settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new penalty-weight sweep tests how explicit Wasserstein regularization affects accuracy and uncertainty on clean and corrupted inputs. Earlier analyses of sampling, momentum, temperature scaling, feature learning, and parametrization are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark averages over five seeds and 95% confidence intervals over five initializations in the feature-learning experiments. The added figures use error bars without introducing a different statistical procedure or reporting an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Figures S13–S14 add GVI error, NLL, and ECE results across five penalty weights. They show broadly similar or worse GVI accuracy, with some weights improving uncertainty metrics. Existing experimental values and plotted results are retained; Figure 1's color change does not alter its results.

T1.justification: Section S3.3.4 adds a short KKT-based stationarity argument for the penalized objective in Equation S123. Although Section 3.2 already asserted an equivalence with penalized GVI, this mathematical justification is new. The original assumptions, theorems, and proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about implicit regularization, the linear-model connection to generalized VI, parametrization and hyperparameter transfer, and competitive generalization with low computational overhead.

C2.justification: The explanations of implicit bias, temperature scaling, learning-rate sensitivity, and pretrained-model behavior under maximal update parametrization are retained, as are the stated limitations. The added GVI discussion reports comparative trends without a distinct new mechanism explanation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: v3 identifies the added comparator as low-rank GVI, specifies its five penalty weights, and refers to Section 5 for its experimental configuration. Existing implementation details, hardware information, and code-access disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 85 cited works and substantive related-work discussion are retained. Wasserstein-regularized generalized VI was already positioned as closely related in Section 3.5; the new experiment does not redefine that relationship.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section S3.3.4 and makes limited grammar, punctuation, heading, and author/header edits. It also removes the broken reference clause in Figure S8's caption. The main narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures S13–S14, recolors the GVI curve in Figure 1, and adopts ICLR typography, headers, and spacing. Existing figures and Table S1 are retained, with some figure and accompanying-text placement changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's toy GVI illustration, Figures S13–S14 provide a useful benchmark comparison with the explicit regularizer motivating IBVI and expose its accuracy–uncertainty tradeoff. This yields a limited empirical improvement. The added KKT paragraph does not reconcile its loss-minimizer description with Section 4.2's rescaled classification result, limiting its theoretical value.
